title: Key-Takeaway & Sub-Concept Coverage (no gaps, no scope creep)
description: The generated TR doc must teach EVERY key takeaway of the session as per the curriculum AND the exam-testable sub-concepts inside each one, and must NOT introduce scope beyond them. A syllabus line names a topic, not its scope, so this is checked against the doc's `coverage_map` — the enumeration the doc must emit, mapping each sub-concept to the slide teaching it or to a named deferral. The map is VERIFIED, not trusted: a thin map that restates the takeaway, or one pointing at a slide that does not teach that sub-concept, fails.
criterion: Every takeaway has a coverage_map entry with the sub-concepts an exam would test; every sub-concept resolves to a slide that genuinely teaches it, or to an explicitly named deferral; nothing is taught outside the takeaway set.

rubric.5: All takeaways and their standard sub-concepts covered, coverage_map accurate; zero scope creep.
rubric.3: All covered but one sub-concept is thin, or one minor out-of-scope aside.
rubric.1: A takeaway or a commonly-tested sub-concept is missing (silently, or behind a map entry that does not hold up), or a whole section is out of scope.

cases.rationale: 1:1 mapping, all five covered, nothing extra.
'Congestion control' takeaway is missing — must fail (gap).
QUIC/HTTP-3 is out of scope for this session — scope creep, must fail.

The map looks complete but the CAUSES (first-reference/demand-load, swapped-out, copy-on-write, illegal access) and minor-vs-major faults are absent — the silent-omission failure this set exists to catch.
